# Intake brief: Evaluate increasing local context size (ctx-size) to serve >65K-token prompts locally

## Problem statement

The local Qwen3 slot's effective context is far smaller than the routing configuration assumes. With `[Qwen3] ctx-size = 262144` in models.ini and 6 slots (day schedule), each slot gets ~43.7K tokens of context (262144/6); at night (8 slots) ~32.8K. The routing thresholds (cold 60K / warm 100K) are clamped to that per-slot context, so any prompt above ~43.7K tokens is forced remote. Usage data shows most sessions exceed this: median session peak context 53,984, mean 72,641, and 60.6% of sessions peak above 43.7K. The original "65K ctx" premise of this item is stale (the 65K value in a `[global]` section was never applied — see LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1). The question is whether raising the per-slot context (by cutting slots within the 262144 native ceiling, and/or other levers) yields more sessions that run fully local without remote fallback, and at what latency/memory/concurrency cost.

## Users

Primary: the operator (rgardler) who runs the local llama-proxy on the Strix Halo iGPU, plus the pi agent sessions that depend on it. Benefit: more sessions stay local (lower latency, no remote cost, privacy), fewer fallback-induced stalls and truncations.

- As an operator, I want the majority of my pi sessions to run fully local (no fallback to remote deepseek), so that local-model utilization is high and remote costs/latency drop.
- As an operator, I want a data-backed recommendation on the slot-count vs per-slot-context tradeoff (e.g. 6×43.7K, 4×65.5K, 3×87.4K, 2×131K) before changing production config, since a wrong choice would either truncate big prompts or starve concurrent sessions.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Benchmark data**: prefill throughput (t/s), TTFT and P95 are measured for representative prompt sizes (~30K/60K/90K/120K tokens) at the baseline (6 slots × ~43.7K) and at least two candidate configs (e.g. 4×~65.5K and 3×~87.4K) using the `proxy/benchmarks` harness; results recorded as a benchmark JSON + summary in the work item.
2. **KV-cache memory**: memory per slot is measured/estimated at each candidate ctx (llama-server metrics, `/props`, rocm-smi/admin metrics) and compared against available headroom; the "~71GB available" claim from the original description is verified or corrected.
3. **Session-retention projection**: using the proxy-usage reports (`~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` + CSVs; 379 sessions in the eval-window report 2026-08-01 19:52 → 08-02 19:52 — the report regenerates daily, e.g. 302 sessions in 2026-08-24), the share of sessions that would stay fully local (no fallback) is computed for each candidate config vs the current baseline by the F5 child (LP-0MSC95W7M009VMEM, proxy/benchmarks/project_session_retention.py — per-config full-local share vs baseline, day/night schedules, persistence-cap 12288 vs raised variants), and the recommendation (F6 go/no-go, parent comment LP-C0MSEGPGJZ006RFTX) maximizes full-local sessions (operator goal — slot reduction acceptable if it increases full-local sessions overall).
4. **Recommendation artifact**: a written go/no-go recommendation with: chosen slots×ctx, updated `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold` / `warm_cache_threshold` values, the interplay with `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens` (KV persistence is currently skipped above 12,288 prompt tokens — LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO), and expected change in fallback rate. Implementation/rollout, if adopted, is tracked as a separate follow-up work item (out of scope here).
5. **Validation & docs**: benchmark runs are reproducible via `proxy/benchmarks`; the full project test suite passes; all related documentation (models.ini comments, proxy/config.yaml comments, benchmark README, docs/llama-router.md as applicable) is updated to reflect the findings and any corrected context assumptions.

> Note: CHANGELOG.md is excluded from the docs requirement — it is managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Model-native context ceiling: Qwen3 `ctx-size = 262144`; per-slot = 262144 / active slots. Rope-scaling beyond native is not assumed to be in scope; if considered, quality degradation must be flagged as a risk, not silently accepted.
- Slot pool must stay aligned with llama-server `--parallel` and the `slot_schedule` (6 day / 8 night) via `session_slot_pool_size` (LP-0MSAOQTJT000S722 deliberately raised slots 4→6 for contention; the evaluation must trade this against capacity).
- Output-token headroom is reserved below the per-slot context; effective usable context is per-slot minus completion headroom (provider.py clamp, LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1).
- `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens: 12288` skips slot save/restore above 12.3K prompt tokens; larger contexts are never persisted, so warm-cache reuse only happens within a slot lease. This interacts directly with any ctx increase.
- Evaluation must not destabilize the live proxy: candidate configs measured via `--ctx-size` overrides / dedicated benchmark runs; production restart only if a rollout is separately approved.
- The 150K–480K prompt sub-cluster of HTTP 400 fallbacks is tracked in LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K and is out of scope (no feasible local ctx covers it).

## Existing state

- **PRODUCTION CHANGE APPLIED 2026-08-02 (operator decision, Option C — see comment LP-C0MSCA9RF1007OAQQ):** models.ini `[Qwen3] ctx-size = 131072`; config.yaml `local_model_ctx_size: 131072`, `session_slot_pool_size: 3`, schedule entries both →3 slots (uniform day/night); `start-llama.sh` router now passes `--threads 8`. Running: `--parallel 3` → per-slot ~43.7K (same day capacity as before; night improved from 32.8K). Effective routing threshold = 131072/3 − 4096 = **39594**.
- Prior state (historical): models.ini `[Qwen3] ctx-size = 262144`; config.yaml `local_model_ctx_size: 262144`, cold threshold 60000, warm threshold 100000, `session_slot_pool_size: 6`, schedule 23:59→8 / 10:00→6, `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens: 12288`; router `--parallel 6` → per-slot ~43.7K day / ~32.8K night.
- **Key operational finding:** an intermediate change to ctx 65536 with 6 slots collapsed the routing threshold to 6826 (65536//6 − 4096) and forced ALL traffic remote via `warm_cache_bypass` — any future ctx/slot change must keep models.ini ctx, `local_model_ctx_size`, `session_slot_pool_size` and the schedule mutually consistent.
- Routing clamp (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`): effective thresholds = min(configured, per-slot ctx − headroom); oversized prompts fall through to remote before context exhaustion.
- 24h usage report (2026-08-01 19:52 → 08-02 19:52, 379 sessions): 76.0% of sessions fell back local→remote; fallback reasons — warm_cache_bypass 55.4%, local_concurrency_limit 18.4%, local_lease_active 12.4%, HTTP 400 9.0%, large_context_bypass 4.6%, slot_exhaustion 0.1%. Session peak-context: median 53,984 / mean 72,641 / p90 149,077 / max 480,381; 60.6% of sessions peak > 43.7K, 38.9% > 65.5K, 23.0% > 87.4K.

## Desired change

Produce the evaluation and recommendation for the FURTHER step. **Note: the operator overrode the original "no production config change" scope on 2026-08-02 and directed Option C (3×~43.7K, ctx 131072) to be implemented immediately — it is live (see comment LP-C0MSCA9RF1007OAQQ).** The remaining deliverable is benchmark data, memory accounting, and a session-retention projection for the candidate configs that raise per-slot context further (4×65.5K / 3×87.4K / 2×131K), plus a written go/no-go recommendation for that further step. The original "if go" condition for C has been satisfied; F6 now recommends whether to go beyond C.

## Key Files:

- `models.ini` — `[Qwen3] ctx-size = 262144`; the ceiling that constrains per-slot context.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `local_model_ctx_size`, `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`, `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`, `session_slot_pool_size`, `slot_schedule`, `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — large-context routing clamp (`per_slot = ctx_size // slots`, effective threshold = min(configured, per-slot − headroom)).
- `proxy/benchmarks/run_benchmark.py`, `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — existing benchmark harness for TTFT/throughput/memory measurement.
- `docs/llama-router.md` — router/context documentation updated by AC 5.
- `start-llama.sh` — derives `LLAMA_PARALLEL` from `session_slot_pool_size`; `--ctx-size` override point for candidate runs.
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`, `daytime_sessions.csv`, `nighttime_sessions.csv` — the 24h usage data used for the session-retention projection.

## Related work

- LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 — models.ini `[global]` ctx-size never applied; established the per-slot clamp. The "65K" premise of this item is corrected by that finding.
- LP-0MSAOQTJT000S722 — raised cold-cache threshold 30K→60K and slot pool 4→6; the slot-count side of the tradeoff.
- LP-0MQMH0GJR001NG0B — centralized quantization/ctx-size in models.ini (plumbing for any future change).
- LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K — HTTP 400 fallback cluster; deferred the 150K–480K prompt sub-cluster to this item (related-to).
- LP-0MSAU6MKS008K0RJ — proxy usage analysis skill that produces `~/proxy-usage-reports/` (data source).
- LP-0MRGUJ3QR002K18G — slot release on remote fallback (concurrency behavior relevant to the slot-count tradeoff).
- LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO — slot persistence safeguards (`session_slot_max_prompt_tokens` interplay).
- LP-0MQMH11AO002IIID — GPU VRAM/ROCm metrics in Prometheus/Grafana; provides the memory-measurement tooling for AC 2.
- LP-0MRO1CM5A008R2KX — proxy progress logging only monitored slot 0; relevant if per-slot monitoring is needed during candidate benchmarks.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Stale premise (known)**: the item's "currently 65000 ctx" is wrong; the real baseline is ~43.7K/slot (6 slots). ACs reference the verified baseline; a follow-up context correction is part of this intake.
- **Contention tradeoff**: cutting slots (6→4→3) may raise `local_concurrency_limit`/`local_lease_active` fallbacks (49% of session fallbacks today). Net full-local session gain must be measured, not assumed.
- **warm_cache_bypass dominance**: 55.4% of fallbacks are warm-cache bypass; because `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens=12288` prevents persistence above 12.3K, bigger ctx may not help cold sessions unless the persistence cap or lease-warmth behavior is also considered — the recommendation must address this.
- **Memory headroom**: "~71GB available" is unverified (rocm-smi reports limited VRAM on this iGPU setup); must be re-measured during the evaluation.
- **Rope-scaling**: beyond-native context extension degrades output quality and is out of scope unless explicitly requested.
- **Scope-creep guard**: implementation/rollout, HTTP 400 sub-cluster, and any persistence-cap changes are tracked as separate work items, not expanded here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should closing this item include implementing the change (models.ini/config edit, restart, monitor) once benchmarks justify it, or is the deliverable an evaluation + recommendation (benchmark data, slot/ctx tradeoff analysis, go/no-go), with implementation tracked as a separate work item?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "Evaluation and recommendation." Source: interactive reply. Impact: AC 4 explicitly excludes rollout; any adoption spawns a follow-up implementation item.
- Q2: "Raising per-slot ctx >65K requires cutting slots (e.g. 4×65.5K or 3×87.4K) unless rope-scaling beyond 262144 is considered. Is reducing the day slot pool acceptable, or is rope-scaling / KV-quantization also in scope to keep 6 slots?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "The goal is maximum number of full sessions on local models (no fallback to remote) — if that means a slot reduction then so be it." Source: interactive reply. Impact: AC 3 optimizes for full-local session count; slot reduction explicitly permitted.
- Q3: "Should the target be ~65-70K/slot (covers the 69.5K median remote prompt) or ~90-100K/slot (covers the 90.7K mean)? This determines whether 4 slots suffice or 2-3 slots / rope-scaling are required." — Answer (operator, interactive): "Review the scaling reports from the usage reporting skill." Source: interactive reply + `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` (2026-08-02 19:52, 379 sessions). Research summary: session peak-context median 53,984 / mean 72,641 / p90 149,077; 60.6% of sessions peak > 43.7K, 38.9% > 65.5K, 23.0% > 87.4K, 13.3% > 131K. AC 3 grounds the target in these distributions rather than a fixed number; the recommendation picks the config maximizing full-local sessions.

---

# Evaluation: Revisit 3×262144 ctx config vs alternatives given 2026-08-26 load evidence (fast & cheap modes)

## Problem statement

On 2026-08-18 the operator superseded the long-context NO-GO (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM / LP-0MSEGPO77005CYCQ had chosen Option C = 3×43.7K because "concurrency is the binding constraint") and accepted **fast mode 3×262144** (per-slot ~87.4K) via LP-0MSY0SDAS0031Y7F, primarily because remote opencode tiers were 429-rate-limited. Today's evidence shows the tradeoff biting:

- Per-slot 87.4K is now *too small for the sessions being served* (sessions at 185K estimated tokens — ratio 2.22) yet large enough to encourage futile ~85K-token prefills every turn (max observed 85,724 tokens; 42.7 M prefill tokens/day).
- The iGPU's shared-memory bandwidth saturates: single 85K prefill collapses concurrent decode to 0.14–0.2 t/s; `/v1/status` p50 1.9s; 280 backend 503s in hour 22.
- 3 slots + giant prefills = `available_slots=0` for long stretches → 4,541 fallbacks/day (concurrency-limited), i.e. the reasoning behind the supersede (avoid remote) is now failing anyway.

The original evaluation's config space (4×65.5K / 3×87.4K / 2×131K / Option C 3×43.7K) needs revisiting with the new session-size distribution and remote-tier status.

## Evaluation required before planning (plan of action only after this completes)

Conduct a full data-backed evaluation of the slots×ctx configuration space and produce a written recommendation BEFORE any implementation plan. Evaluation MUST produce separate recommendations for:

- **fast mode** (fallbacks OK, speed important): the best slots×ctx balance for speed — more slots (concurrency, less prefill starvation) vs larger per-slot ctx (more sessions fit); re-run the F5 session-retention projection (LP-0MSC95W7M009VMEM) with 2026-08-24→26 usage; include decode-stall cost of giant prefills in the TTFT model rather than only "sessions that fit".
- **cheap mode** (fallbacks to be avoided, cost reduction important): 2×262144 (131,072/slot) is the current cheap shape — evaluate whether slot count / ctx should differ and whether the cheap static clamp 61,440 / scheduled 100,000 remains right; the F5-style projection must maximize sessions that stay local in cheap WITHOUT remote spend.

Analysis inputs: `~/proxy-usage-reports` (session context distribution, fallback rates, mode windows), `proxy/benchmarks` harness (prefill throughput at 30K/60K/90K/120K prompts — reuse LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM F2/F3/F5 artifacts), `rocm-smi`/`/props` memory figures (context ~47 GB at 262144 with headroom), and the 2026-08-26 incident logs.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Config-space benchmark**: measured prefill t/s, TTFT, P95 and KV memory for current 3×262144 vs at least 2 candidates (e.g. Option C 3×131072 and 2×131072 or 4×131072) via the benchmark harness; recorded as benchmark JSON + summary.
2. **Session-retention projection**: re-run full-local session share for each candidate per mode (fast/cheap) on the 2026-08-24→26 session data; include the *decode-stall penalty* of oversized prefills in the scoring, not just "fits in slot".
3. **Remote-tier status report**: current opencode usage limits / 429 behavior (does the supersede's premise still hold?) as a factor in the recommendation.
4. **Mode-specific recommendation**: chosen slots×ctx (may differ fast vs cheap), updated `local_model_ctx_size`, clamps and `slot_schedule` pins, expected fallback-rate and P95 change per mode; explicit go/no-go vs keeping 3×262144.
5. **No config change without approval**: evaluation and plan only; rollout (if adopted) as a separate follow-up with a restart plan.
6. **Validation**: reproducible benchmark runs; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Model-native ceiling 262144; rope-scaling not assumed in scope.
- Must stay aligned with `session_slot_pool_size`, `slot_schedule`, and llama-server `--parallel`.
- Evaluation must not destabilize the live proxy (dedicated benchmark runs / ctx overrides only).

# Evaluation: Proactive session compaction for oversized contexts (fast & cheap modes)

## Problem statement

Today (2026-08-26) the proxy logged **2,296 `context_pressure` warnings** — more than 2× the ~1,200/day of Aug 24–25 — with sessions at `estimated_tokens=185,218` against `per_slot_ctx=83,285` (**ratio 2.22 ≥ 0.80 warn ratio**). Long-lived audit/implement sessions accumulate multi-hundred-K-token histories that can never fit a local slot. These sessions are the root cause of the dominant slowdown pattern: every local turn triggers a full ~85K-token re-prefill (85,724 max observed; 42.7 M prefill tokens in one day), monopolizes all 3 slots, collapses concurrent decode to 0.14–0.2 t/s, and drives the fallback storm (4,541 fallbacks + 280 backend 503s in hour 22).

The `context_pressure` warning already suggests compaction but nothing enforces or automates it. A prior experiment design exists but is **blocked** (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ "validate session compaction gains without quality loss").

## Evaluation required before planning (plan of action only after this completes)

Conduct a full data-backed evaluation of proactive compaction (prompt-history truncation/TCX-style summarization of the oldest turns, or hard remote-routing of sessions whose estimated context exceeds the per-slot capacity) and produce a written recommendation BEFORE any implementation plan. Evaluation MUST produce separate recommendations for:

- **fast mode** (fallbacks OK, speed important): compaction threshold and aggressiveness that maximize local speed (TTFT/P95); trade-off of compaction frequency vs quality; whether compaction should be automatic on `context_pressure` breach or advisory.
- **cheap mode** (fallbacks to be avoided, cost reduction important): whether proactive compaction (vs remote fallback) is the ONLY acceptable path for oversized sessions, since cheap must minimize remote spend; define the cheap-mode line between "compact and serve local" vs "reject/queue".

Analysis inputs: `~/proxy-usage-reports` session-context distributions (median 53,984 / mean 72,641 per LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM earlier data; re-derive from 2026-08-24/25/26 reports), `context_pressure` warning logs, blocked experiment LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ (unblock or reference), the proxy's existing compaction tooling from LP-0MSDCLQ2W001LGWC, and the 2026-08-26 incident logs.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Evidence write-up**: distribution of session estimated-context sizes and how many sessions breach the per-slot cap per mode (fast 87.4K-slot/83,285 clamp; cheap 2×262144 → 131,072/slot, static clamp 61,440) in the 2026-08-24→26 reports; correlation between oversized sessions and the decode stalls/fallbacks logged.
2. **Compaction design options**: 2–3 candidate compaction strategies (summarize-oldest-turns, hard cap + auto-truncate, hybrid with remote) each with quality-risk notes, referencing/reviving LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ where valid.
3. **Mode-specific recommendation** (fast and cheap separately): chosen strategy per mode, trigger thresholds (context_pressure ratio / absolute tokens), and expected effect on fallback rate, local utilization, and remote cost.
4. **No behavior change without approval**: evaluation and plan only; follow-up work item for implementation once approved.
5. **Validation**: analysis scripts/reports committed; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Evaluation must not destabilize the live proxy.
- Compaction must not silently drop content the operator needs — quality-loss risk must be quantified or flagged, not assumed away.
- Interaction with slot save/restore (compacted sessions should restore efficiently) and with the hard-routing-cap companion item must be addressed.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MR5MAJNM005R905** – Fix fallback chain queuing: bypass queue on local slot busy, local-only concurrency=1, add slot release time logging (completed)
- **LP-0MSUDLRIN003Q76E** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/skill/audit/scripts/verify_context_reduction.py:357 — Unused `noqa` directive (non-enabled: `BLE001`, `S110`) (RUF100) (completed)
- **LP-0MSUDLRM10036Q6P** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/skill/audit/scripts/verify_context_reduction.py:357 — Unused `noqa` directive (non-enabled: `BLE001`, `S110`) (RUF100) (completed)

- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absolute, acceptance, accumulate, action, addressed (+180 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absolute, acceptance, accumulate, action, addressed (+180 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absolute, acceptance, accumulate, action, addressed (+180 more)

# Evaluation: KV slot save/restore reuse gap and `/slots` 500 storms (fast & cheap modes)

## Problem statement

Slot persistence is failing to do its job, forcing full re-prefill every turn:

- **~95% of context checkpoints are never reused**: In `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log` (2026-08-26), 2,954 checkpoints saved vs only 145 restored. 22 `slot_*.bin` snapshots (100–560 MB each) written to `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache` between 22:02–23:09, mostly unreferenced.
- **`GET /slots` returns HTTP 500 ~9% of the time**: 6,459 of ~69.6K polls today returned 500, plus 527 HTTP 400. `slots_stale=true` in most proxy status lines — the proxy's slot-state view is unreliable, breaking session↔slot affinity and cascading into `local_concurrency_limit` fallbacks.
- **Persistence skipped for oversized sessions**: Proxy-side persistence is disabled above `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens` cap (≈83,285 tokens; LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO) — exactly the sessions that need reuse (giant contexts) never get persistence.
- **Result**: 42.7M prefill tokens/day, decode collapse to 0.14–0.2 t/s, 4,541 fallbacks (2026-08-26).

**Historical context**: Earlier slot save/restore ReadTimeouts under concurrent load were tracked (LP-0MSI1RWLM007N367), and llama-server's native context checkpoints exist — the gap is in the restore path / affinity.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root-cause write-up**: Why checkpoints are saved but not restored (affinity breaks, `slots_stale`, size gating, 500s, lease churn) with log-based evidence and timeline correlation to the 2026-08-26 incident.
2. **Restore-reuse metric**: Current restore rate quantified (~5%) and a target restore rate per mode with fix options ranked by expected prefill-token savings.
3. **`/slots` 500 triage**: Root cause of the 500s (router-mode proxying, slot out-of-range during prefill, etc.) and fix options; correlation of 500s with concurrent giant prefills.
4. **Mode-specific recommendation**: Selected fix set + persistence-cap/threshold values for fast and cheap separately, with expected fallback-rate and TTFT/P95 impact.
5. **No code change without approval**: Evaluation and plan only; implementation tracked as a follow-up work item.
6. **Validation**: Reproducible analysis scripts; full project test suite passes with no regressions.

## Constraints

- Do not destabilize the live proxy; evaluate from logs/metrics only.
- Save/restore must not wedge the GPU (the reason for the size gate in LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO) — any cap raise must carry a timeout/cooldown plan.
- Evaluation must produce separate recommendations for:
  - **Fast mode** (fallbacks OK, speed important): prioritize TTFT/P95 improvement from reliable incremental reuse on large sessions.
  - **Cheap mode** (fallbacks to be avoided, cost reduction important): prioritize local utilization — reliable restore is the lever that keeps oversized sessions local without full re-prefill.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_build_slot_context`, `_slot_persistence_enabled`, `_slot_persistence_skip_when_busy`, persistence gating logic
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log` — checkpoint create/restore events, slot lifecycle
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` — `slots_stale`, orphan/lease events, HTTP 500/400 on `/slots`
- `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache/` — slot snapshot inventory
- `ds4/` — proxy mode configuration (fast/cheap)

## Related Work

- **LP-0MSI1RWLM007N367** (completed): Slot save/restore ReadTimeouts persist under concurrent load (~1.8% of saves). Root-cause: concurrent saves cause timeouts → led to load-aware gating.
- **LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO** (completed): Slot save/restore ReadTimeouts wedge the GPU. Root-cause: large context saves (~2GB KV cache) wedge GPU → led to context-size gating cap.
- **LP-0MSHW2AXJ009DO3S** (completed): Fix /slots endpoint query — llama-server returns HTTP 400 without `?model=`.
- **LP-0MSI5B1T2009GQ4C** (completed): Load-aware save gating + timeout rebalance.
- **LP-0MSVP7XJ6008QPKX** (completed): GET /slots returns HTTP 500 after cheap-mode restart.
- **LP-0MSB0RV72001KNRV** (completed): Slot registry leak: `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` never frees `_slot_owners`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: The only viable fix may conflict with GPU-wedge constraints from LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO. Mitigation: evaluate timeout/cooldown plans before recommending cap changes.
- **Risk**: Fast vs cheap cap thresholds may converge to the same value. Mitigation: document if modes cannot be differentiated.
- **Assumption**: llama-server native checkpoint format is compatible across restarts (to be verified).
- **Scope-creep alert**: The `/slots` 500s and slot registry leak are related but separate bugs. This evaluation covers them as root-cause factors for the reuse gap, but fixes for those are tracked separately.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: What are the exact fast and cheap mode configurations? — A: Defined in `ds4/` directory; fast mode tolerates fallbacks for speed, cheap mode prioritizes local utilization. Source: work item description (herdr log analysis).
- Q: Is the `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens` cap the only persistence blocker? — A: No. Load-aware gating (LP-0MSI1RWLM007N367 F3) also blocks saves when slots are busy. Context-size gating blocks the sessions that need it most. Source: `proxy/proxy/session.py` `_build_slot_context` and related work.

data.description:
# Rollout: raise local persistence cap to routing clamp — 83,285 (fast) / 126,976 (cheap)

## Problem Statement

The persistence cap (`session_slot_max_prompt_tokens`) is the binding constraint on local session reuse. Currently at a 12,288-token effective cap, sessions that fit the per-slot routing clamp (83,285 fast / 126,976 cheap) but exceed 12.3K tokens lose warm-cache KV restore, forcing full cold re-prefills every turn. This causes 42.7M prefill tokens/day, iGPU shared-memory bandwidth saturation, `available_slots=0` stretches, and 4,541 fallbacks/day.

Raising the cap to the routing clamp is projected to increase fully-local sessions from 61.9% → 89.1% (F5 projection on 2026-08-24→26 data).

## User Stories

- **As a proxy operator**, I want all context-eligible sessions to restore from warm KV cache so that cold prefill load is minimized and iGPU bandwidth is not saturated.
- **As an LLM user**, I want faster response times by avoiding unnecessary cold re-prefills when my session already has a warm KV cache.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Config values set**: `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens` set to 83,285 in `proxy/config.yaml` (fast mode) and 126,976 in `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (cheap mode), with comments documenting the derivation (`local_model_ctx_size // active_slots − 4096`).
2. **Config validated at startup**: No min routing clamp warnings; the persistence cap is never above the routing clamp (no dead-band). Existing startup validation confirmed working with new values.
3. **Staged rollout executed**: dev/staging tested first, proxy verified healthy (slots probe OK, /v1/models OK), then controlled production restart window. Rollback plan = revert cap to 0 (dynamic) and restart.
4. **Post-rollout metrics collected**: 48h of warm vs cold prefill ratio, fallback rate, remote spend, TTFT distribution, `available_slots=0` frequency — compared against 2026-08-26 baseline and recorded in a comment on this work item. (Instrumentation via LP-0MTBTCK2I005MOTE.)
5. **Tests pass**: Full project test suite passes; reproducible config diff shown (before/after).

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Risk**: Raising the cap increases memory used per persisted session. Mitigation: iGPU shared memory is the binding resource; the cap increase (12K → 83K/127K) is bounded by the routing clamp which is already considered safe by the router.
- **Risk**: Config mismatch between modes after rollout. Mitigation: staged rollout on dev/staging first; verify both modes independently.
- **Risk**: Rollback needed. Mitigation: revert cap to 0 (dynamic) and restart — fast, no code change.
- **Scope-creep risk**: Changes to cheap-mode slot shape (LP-0MTBTCTE8007E6VU) are out of scope; if the cheap shape changes, the 126,976 cap value remains the same per-slot clamp.

## Constraints

- Must not destabilize the live proxy: staged rollout, rollback plan = revert cap to 0 (dynamic) and restart.
- Slot save/restore circuit breaker (max 3 consecutive failures, 300s cooldown) and load-aware skip (`session_slot_skip_when_busy`) remain unchanged.
- No change to model-native ceiling 262144 / rope scaling.
- `local_model_ctx_size: 262144` and `session_slot_pool_size: 3` (fast) unchanged.
- `slot_schedule` pins unchanged — no slots×ctx change.

## Rollout Plan

1. **Dev**: Set config values, restart proxy, verify slots probe + /v1/models OK.
2. **Staging**: Repeat; collect 24h of metrics.
3. **Production**: Controlled restart during low-traffic window; monitor for 48h.
4. **Rollback**: Revert cap to 0 in both config files, restart proxy. < 1 minute.

## Existing State

- `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens: 0` (dynamic derivation) in both `proxy/config.yaml` and `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`.
- Dynamic derivation: `effective_per_slot_threshold(local_model_ctx_size // active_slots - 4096)`.
- Current config: `local_model_ctx_size: 262144`, 3 slots (fast schedule 23:59→3, cheap schedule 10:00→3).
- Related completed work: LP-0MSEQR964003C30S (dynamic derivation), LP-0MSEGPO77005CYCQ (ctx-size follow-up), LP-0MSEQR04J007OCGH (tests: clamp-derived persistence cap).
- Related open work: LP-0MTBTCTE8007E6VU (cheap-mode slot shape decision), LP-0MTBTCK2I005MOTE (post-rollout monitoring).
- Discovery source: LP-0MTAQNAIO0069DUP (ctx-config evaluation, commit a866aa1 to dev).

## Desired Change

Set explicit static values:
- `proxy/config.yaml` (fast mode): `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens: 83285`
- `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (cheap mode): `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens: 126976`

Derivation: `local_model_ctx_size (262144) // active_slots - 4096` → 83,285 (fast, 3 slots) / 126,976 (cheap, 2 slots per pending shape decision LP-0MTBTCTE8007E6VU).

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — Fast mode persistence cap (set to 83285)
- `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — Cheap mode persistence cap (set to 126976)
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — Persistence gating logic (read-only; no code change)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `effective_per_slot_threshold()` derivation function (read-only; no code change)

## Related Work

- **LP-0MTAQNAIO0069DUP** — ctx-config evaluation (discovery source)
- **LP-0MSEQR964003C30S** — Dynamic session_slot_max_prompt_tokens from per-slot clamp (completed; established dynamic derivation)
- **LP-0MSEGPO77005CYCQ** — ctx-size evaluation follow-up (completed; routing-estimate fix + persistence-cap raise to 3x43.7K)
- **LP-0MTBTCK2I005MOTE** — Post-rollout proxy monitoring (open; covers AC4 metrics collection)
- **LP-0MTBTCTE8007E6VU** — Decide cheap-mode slot shape (open; determines cheap-mode cap value — 126,976 based on 2×262144 pending decision)
- **LP-0MSEQR04J007OCGH** — Tests: clamp-derived persistence cap + multiplier consistency (completed)

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Why set explicit values instead of keeping dynamic derivation? — A: The evaluation found the dynamic derivation was producing 12,288 (not the full routing clamp), limiting warm-cache benefits. The dynamic derivation formula (`ctx_size // slots - 4096`) at current config (262144/3) gives 83,285, but the effective cap observed was lower — setting explicit values ensures the full routing clamp is respected regardless of schedule changes. (Agent assessment from LP-0MTAQNAIO0069DUP analysis.)
- Q: Does the proxy support per-mode override for `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens`? — A: Yes, via separate config files (`config.yaml` for fast, `config-cheap.yaml` for cheap). No code change needed.
- Q: Is the cheap-mode slot shape (2×262144 vs 3×131072) decided? — A: No — LP-0MTBTCTE8007E6VU is open. This rollout uses 126,976 (matching current 2×262144 shape). If the shape changes to 3×131072, the cap value (126,976) would remain the same since both shapes produce the same per-slot clamp.
data.title: Rollout: raise local persistence cap (session_slot_max_prompt_tokens) to routing clamp
